title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: Why do we keep the heap size exactly at \(k\)?
teacher_message:
```text
nums → [largest, …, kth largest] | [smaller values]
             ← exactly k values →
```

We keep exactly `k` values because the target is the value in position `k` when `nums` is ordered from largest to smallest. Those `k` values are the current top-`k` candidates; the smallest among them is the boundary—the kth largest value seen so far.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: The learner asks why the heap size is k but does not state the rank target.

model_assessment.rationale: The message is a question and does not demonstrate the target rank or its relationship to k.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: When we see a new number, do we remove the smallest if the heap grows past \(k\)?
teacher_message:
```text
new value → heap
             ↓
   exceeds capacity? ── yes → remove heap[0]
             ↓
       heap stays bounded
       heap[0] = smallest retained value
```

Yes. Add the new value first. If `heap` exceeds its fixed capacity, remove `heap[0]`, the root. Because the root is the smallest retained value, this keeps the strongest retained candidates.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Asks whether to remove the smallest value when the heap exceeds k, without explaining the root invariant.

model_assessment.rationale: The message is a question about the procedure and does not itself demonstrate that the min-heap root is the smallest retained value.

title: Kth Largest Element
problem: Find the kth largest value using a min-heap of size k.
learner_message: How does the min-heap keep `heap[0]` as the smallest without sorting everything?
teacher_message:
```text
        heap[0]
        /    \
   child   child

parent ≤ each child
        ↓
smallest value stays at the root
```

A min-heap does not sort every value. It only maintains the local rule that each parent is no larger than its children. When `heap` changes, it swaps values along one path until that rule is restored. Because the root is smaller than everything below it, `heap[0]` remains the smallest retained value.

model_diagnosis.decomposition: Asks how the min-heap maintains the smallest retained value at heap[0] without sorting everything.

model_assessment.rationale: The learner asks for an explanation but does not themselves state the root-threshold invariant.
